Per-round 'application, review and face check about 5 minutes' and 'exam 10-15 minutes' are unsourced guesses; the key says there is no official review-time figure

Long: the weekly schedule and pitfalls sections go beyond what was asked

reasons: Both answers lead with the 6-point cap (10 down to 4), reject the 'no longer afraid of deductions' premise (8 more points reaches 12, then licence seizure and full-score study), explain the clearing rule, and give 3 hours of study as the base figure. I checked Articles 17, 18, 25, 26 and 27 of order 163 on gov.cn and the Beijing exam rules. B's extra specifics hold up: 7-day full-score study, the two-full-score-records bar on applying, 60 seconds per question, retake within 24 hours up to 2 times, no banking study time, and the blacklist with a 3-cycle ban for fraud. B also covers on-site study (1 hour for 2 points) and says points cannot be saved up, but it omits the public-activity route, mixing and no fee. A omits every other method, which is a gap against key 5, and gives only a vague 'retake per page prompt'. A is tighter, more honest about review time, and its arithmetic is right. B is noticeably longer and gives some guessed per-round timings. B wins slightly on completeness and actionability, and A on concision.
